content:
Elizabethtown College’s School of Graduate and Professional Studies (SGPS), in collaboration with The Society for UAP Studies (SUAPS), recently launched “Foundations of UAP Studies,” one of the first college-credit courses dedicated to the interdisciplinary academic study of unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP). The online course begins in spring 2027 and will examine UAP through historical, cultural, psychological, philosophical, and scientific perspectives.

The three-credit course will be co-taught by Dr. Michael D. Silberstein, co-founder and Secretary of the Society for UAP Studies and Elizabethtown College Professor of Philosophy and Professor of Science, Society, and Technology, along with alumnus Dr. Michael C. Cifone ’00, co-founder and president of the Society for UAP Studies and founding editor of Limina: the Journal of UAP Studies. 

“UAP studies present an important opportunity for interdisciplinary academic inquiry,” Silberstein said. “Bringing this subject into a college curriculum creates a structured environment for critical thinking and serious scholarly engagement.”

UAPs have received increased attention from government agencies, scientific institutions, and policymakers in recent years. Developments include the public release of federal UAP records, congressional hearings featuring witness testimony, NASA’s independent UAP study, and the establishment of the Department of Defense’s All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO), which investigates reports of UAP. 

The course will examine the subject within an academic setting, emphasizing research, evidence, and critical analysis. From an interdisciplinary perspective, students will explore all aspects of UFO/UAP related phenomena from their beginnings to current-day events. 

The curriculum draws on primary sources, government documents, scientific reports, academic literature, and well-known guest experts. Students will participate in collaborative research and develop an independently researched final presentation. 

About the Society for UAP Studies

The Society for UAP Studies is an international nonprofit scholarly organization dedicated to advancing rigorous, interdisciplinary research into unidentified anomalous phenomena and establishing UAP studies as a recognized academic field. Through its peer-reviewed journal, “Limina: The Journal of UAP Studies,” international conferences, research initiatives, and university partnerships, SUAPS is developing the scholarly infrastructure necessary to bring UAP research into higher education. Its long-term vision includes expanding academic collaborations, supporting emerging researchers, advancing scientific and philosophical inquiry, and integrating UAP studies into college and university curricula internationally.
